newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-MARSH GRABS TWO-STROKE LEAD AT U.S. SENIOR OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MARSH GRABS TWO-STROKE LEAD AT U.S. SENIOR OPEN.

text.p: Australian Graham Marsh fired his second successive 3-under-par 67 Saturday to grab a two-stroke lead after the third round of the $1.3 million U.S. Senior Open.

While most players struggled to make par at the tough Olympia Fields Country Club course, Marsh has collected 10 birdies over the last two rounds to move to 4-under 206 with 18 holes to play in the year's third major championship on the Senior Tour calendar.
Marsh, who started the day one stroke off the lead, carded five birdies and two bogeys in his third round to open a two-shot lead over South African John Bland, who shot a 1-under 69 Saturday.
Bland was tied for the lead before bogeying the 16th and 17th holes.
Bland and Dave Eichelberger are the only players to record three rounds of par or better. Eichelberger shot even-par 70 to remain within striking distance at 1-under 209.
The rest of the field was above par, led by Senior Tour rookie Hubert Green at 1-over 211 after a third-round 68.

Leonard Thompson and Tom Wargo were at at 2-over 212, one stroke better than Bob Charles, Dana Quigley, Hugh Baiocchi and Jose Maria Canizares, who moved into contention with a 4-under 66 -- the best round of the tournament.
Overnight leader Kermit Zarley soared to a 10-over 80, tumbling out of contention.

The 53-year-old Marsh continued the solid play he began two weeks ago with a third-place finish at the du Maurier Champions event. He won last week's Nationwide Championship and is 26-under over his last 10 rounds.
"It's nice to be in this position," he said. "You have to say you're on a roll. That's what we go out and work for.
"I was very focused on trying to play well in this championship," Marsh said. "That's what I've been working for all year."
Marsh started with a birdie on the first hole, but bogeyed number three. He then picked up three strokes with a run of three birdies over four holes beginning at the par-4 seventh.
A bogey at 12 dropped the Australian back to 3-under, but he picked up his fifth birdie at 13.
"I've been close to it in the Senior Open. In Pinehurst (in 1994), I wasn't that far away," Marsh said. "I was fairly close last year up in Cleveland.
"You have to go out and play well. Any number of players can still win this championship," he said. "A two-shot lead is absolutely nothing."
